title: Project Structure and File Organization
learningObjectives: Choose organization proportionate to project size.
Use descriptive names and clear entry points.
Separate source, tests, assets, docs, and generated content.
Avoid duplicate files and excessive nesting.

understand.concept: Project structure organizes source files, tests, assets, documentation, and configuration so people can locate and understand them. Structure should fit project size: a single-file script may be fine, while a growing application benefits from consistent folders and clear entry points.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear, repeatable practices help beginners make safe changes and understand how work moves from an idea to a checked result.
understand.analogy: A small checklist helps a person complete a task in order without forgetting important steps.
understand.analogyLimit: Software workflows also involve technical tools, dependencies, collaboration, and test evidence, which a checklist analogy cannot fully describe.

explain.narrative: Use purposeful names and one consistent grouping strategy. Keep authored source distinct from generated output or dependencies. Avoid deep folder nesting, duplicate copies, and arbitrary splitting into files that add no useful boundary.
